chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Big Green plays My Buddy as a waltz in a Seventh Avenue gin mill
summary: Danny saw a down-and-out Big Green asked to play, and he improvised on a waltz that earned a standing ovation from other trombonists.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: No. That was where I saw Jabbo. All these people was in a gin mill on Seventh Avenue down in a basement, and I'm in there. And Big Green is in there, and he's drunk, and he'd lost his weight, and he said ain't nobody would hire him after Fletcher, and Chick Webb hired him for a while but he couldn't depend on him...
Big Green the trombone player, yeah..

Yes. And he was this big, tall cat, almost seven feet. But he had once but robust, but his clothes is hangin' on him; you could almost lop his pants from him. And he was foolin' with that smoke, that shit that they used

to drink. Nasty alcohol. Cheap. 25 cents for a little jar they had made like a little cow, and you'd get one of them. I drank some of that, spat it on a wall and messed the paint up. That's how bad this shit was. So all them trombone players was playin', Big Green was sittin' at the bar and listening. And then when Budd... And they were swingin' down there, man! Trombones burnin'. Higgenbotham and all of them.
So they asked Green to play. They said, "Man, play something, man." The bartender said, "Man, why don't you play something?" He had a funny eye...
He had a funny eye, didn't he.
One of his eyes looking this way. So they give him a trombone, and that big, tall son-of-a-bitch got up with his trombone and said, "What you gonna play?" "Play a waltz." [SINGS REFRAIN]...

Yeah. A waltz... They was playing that waltz, and the cat was improvising on it... [SINGS REFRAIN] He played that (?). When they got through, them sumbitches give him a standing ovation. They said, "Leave the master alone." A waltz! I mean, he didn't get in there and... Well, that was his bag, you know...
